Description: The physical science is a branch of science that explore the fundamental principles and natural laws governing the non-living world. They encompass several key disciplines that study the properties and behavior of matter, energy, and the interactions between them.
Synonyms: Physical disciplines, Physical sciences field, Physical sciences sector, Physical sciences research

Description: Life sciences encompass a broad field of scientific study that focuses on living organisms, including plants, animals, and humans. It involves the exploration and understanding of various aspects of life, ranging from the structure and function of cells and organisms to their interactions within ecosystems.
Synonyms: Biological sciences, Biological research, Life sciences and biotechnology, Biosciences, Life science research, Biological studies

Description: Social sciences focuses on subjects like economics, psychology, and history, while the humanities explore philosophy, languages and literature, and the arts.
Synonyms: Southern criminology, Third World criminology, Non-Western criminology, Postcolonial criminology, Decolonial criminology
LCC_name_2: History of scholarship and learning. The humanities

Description: Engineering is the design and construction of systems and structures for influencing the world around us and enhancing our experience within it. Engineers use the fundamental principles of mathematics, physics and chemistry to create machines that enable us to travel faster, provide improved medical care, and process more complicated information.
Synonyms: Engineerings, Engineering

Description: Mathematics and computing is the study and analysis of abstract concepts, such as numbers and patterns. Mathematics is the language of choice for scientifically describing and modelling the universe and everything that happens within it. Computing enables these mathematical problems to be solved in an efficient and automated way.

Materials science is an interdisciplinary field involving the properties of matter and its applications to various areas of science and engineering. It includes elements of applied physics and chemistry, as well as chemical, mechanical, civil and electrical engineering.

Chemistry is a branch of science that involves the study of the composition, structure and properties of matter. Often known as the central science, it is a creative discipline chiefly concerned with atomic and molecular structure and its change, for instance through chemical reactions.
Synonyms: Chemical science, Chemical study, Chemical discipline

Description: Biological sciences encompasses all the divisions of natural sciences examining various aspects of vital processes. The concept includes anatomy, physiology, cell biology, biochemistry and biophysics, and covers all organisms from microorganisms, animals to plants.
Synonyms: Biologic Sciences, Biological Science, Life Sciences, Biologic Science, Life Science, Biological Science Discipline, Biological Science Disciplines

Description: The health sciences study all aspects of health, disease and healthcare. This field of study aims to develop knowledge, interventions and technology for use in healthcare to improve the treatment of patients.

The study and practice of international relations is interdisciplinary in nature, blending the fields of economics, history, and political science to examine topics such as human rights, global poverty, the environment, economics, globalization, security, global ethics, and the political environment.
Synonyms: Political Factors, Decentralization, Political Factor, Liberalism, Political Activities, Conservatism, Political Activity, Voting
German Synonyms: Politikwissenschaft, Internationale Beziehungen, politische Wissenschaft, Politologie

Description: Electrical and electronic engineering is the branch of engineering that makes use of electricity. Electrical engineering concentrates on systems for generating and transmitting large electrical currents and converting them into other forms of energy, such as mechanical motion. Electronic engineering focusses on lower energy currents for processing and communicating information.
Synonyms: Electrical Engineering
DDC_name_1: Electrical, magnetic, optical, communications, computer engineering; electronics, lighting

Description: A collectivity of people sharing interactions, relations and networks, usually in a geographical or physical space and with similarity of purpose or life aims.
Synonyms: Social Science

Description: Pure mathematics uses mathematics to explore abstract ideas, mathematics that does not necessarily describe a real physical system. This can include developing the fundamental tools used by mathematicians, such as algebra and calculus, describing multi-dimensional space, or better understanding the philosophical meaning of mathematics and numbers themselves.

Physics is the search for and application of rules that can help us understand and predict the world around us. Central to physics are ideas such as energy, mass, particles and waves. Physics attempts to both answer philosophical questions about the nature of the universe and provide solutions to technological problems.

Religion is a range of social-cultural systems, including designated behaviors and practices, morals, beliefs, worldviews, texts, sanctified places, prophecies, ethics, or organizations, that generally relate humanity to supernatural, transcendental, and spiritual elements —although there is no scholarly consensus over what precisely constitutes a religion.
Synonyms: Religions, Religious Studies, Religious Belief, Religious Beliefs, Prayers, Religious Ethics, Prayer

Description: History studies the past, including events occurring after the invention of writing systems (dist. 'prehistory'). History relates to past events as well as the memory, discovery, collection, organization, presentation, and interpretation of information about these events.
Synonyms: Historical Aspect, Histories, Historical Aspects

Description: Statistics is the application of mathematical concepts to understanding and analysing large collections of data. A central tenet of statistics is to describe the variations in a data set or population using probability distributions. This analysis aids understanding of what underlies these variations and enables predictions of future changes.

Computer science is the study and development of the protocols required for automated processing and manipulation of data. This includes, for example, creating algorithms for efficiently searching large volumes of information or encrypting data so that it can be stored and transmitted securely..Computational science is a discipline concerned with the design, implementation and use of mathematical models to analyse and solve scientific problems. Typically, the term refers to the use of computers to perform simulations or numerical analysis of a scientific system or process..Information theory and computation is the study and development of protocols and algorithms for solving problems and analysing information. This discipline usually breaks information down into individual bits, and then determines the optimum logical operation required to efficiently process this data in any required way..Information technology is the design and implementation of computer networks for data processing and communication. This includes designing the hardware for processing information and connecting separate components, and developing software that can efficiently and faultlessly analyse and distribute this data.
Synonyms: Computational Molecular Biology, Computational biology, Bio-Informatics, Computing science, Bioinformatics

Description: Psychology is a scientific discipline that focuses on understanding mental functions and the behaviour of individuals and groups.
Synonyms: Psychological Factors, Psychological Side Effects, Psychosocial Factor, Psychologists, Psychological Factor, Psychological Side Effect, Psychosocial Factors, Psychologist, Behavioral Science

Description: Art is a diverse range of human activity, and resulting product, that involves creative or imaginative talent expressive of technical proficiency, beauty, emotional power, or conceptual ideas.
Synonyms: Art

Description: Economics is the study of how people allocate scarce resources for production, distribution, and consumption, both individually and collectively. The two branches of economics are microeconomics and macroeconomics. Economics focuses on efficiency in production and exchange.
Synonyms: Consumer Price Indices, Consumer Price Index, Utility Theory, Macroeconomic Factors, Consumption, Remittance, Cost of Living, Remittances, Economic Policy, Living Cost, Economic Conditions, Production, Capital, Living Costs, Household Consumption

Description: Earth and environmental sciences cover all aspects of Earth and planetary sciences, and broadly encompasses solid Earth processes, surface and atmospheric dynamics, Earth system history, climate and climate change, marine and freshwater systems, and ecology. It also considers the interactions between humans and these systems.
Literature is any collection of written work, but it is also used more narrowly for writings specifically considered to be an art form, especially prose fiction, drama, and poetry.
Synonyms: Article, Biography, Composition, Drama, Essay, History information

Description: Media and communication are closely interconnected fields that involve the creation, transmission, and exchange of information, ideas, and messages. some key aspects of media and communication: Mass Media, Journalism, Digital Media, Advertising and Marketing, Public Relations
Synonyms: Mass Communication, Media Studies, Communication Studies, Journalism and Media
German Synonyms: Medien- und Kommunikationswissenschaft, Medien und Kommunikation

Description: Mechanical engineering is the branch of engineering that deals with moving machines and their components. A central principle of mechanical engineering is the control of energy: transferring it from one form to another to suit a specific demand. Car engines, for example, convert chemical energy into kinetic energy. Sub-areas such as Process (Chemical) or Industrial Engineering have their roots in Mechanical Engineering.

Management (or managing) is the administration of an organization, whether it is a business, a nonprofit organization, or a government body. It is the art and science of managing the resources of the business. Management includes the activities of setting the strategy of an organization and coordinating the efforts of its employees (or of volunteers) to accomplish its objectives through the application of available resources, such as financial, natural, technological, and human resources.
Synonyms: Business, Management

Description: Archaeology is the study of the artefacts and other physical evidence left by past societies of humans and closely related species. It uses scientific analysis of field samples to inform historical understanding.
Synonyms: Archeology

Description: Philosophy is a branch of knowledge and an academic discipline that explores fundamental questions about existence, knowledge, ethics, logic, and the nature of reality. It involves rational inquiry, critical thinking, and systematic analysis to examine and understand concepts and ideas about the world and human experience.
Synonyms: Hedonism, Stoicism, Philosophical Overviews, Philosophical Overview, Philosophies

Description: Cultural studies, also called the cultural sciences, is an interdisciplinary field or scientific branch that examines the dynamics of contemporary culture (including its politics and popular culture) and its historical foundations.
Synonyms: Cultural Background, Customs, Cultural Backgrounds, Belief, Beliefs, Custom, Cultures
LCC_name_1: Study and teaching. Research. Cultural studies

Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language including the study of grammar, syntax, and phonetics. Specific branches of linguistics include sociolinguistics, dialectology, psycholinguistics, computational linguistics, comparative linguistics, and structural linguistics.

Law is a set of rules that are created and are enforceable by social or governmental institutions to regulate behavior, with its precise definition a matter of longstanding debate. It has been variously described as a science and as the art of justice.
Synonyms: Medical Jurisprudence, Litigations, Constitutional Law, Constitutional Laws, State Interests, Court Decisions, Laws, Court Decision, Legal Obligation, Legal Aspects, Legal Aspect, Legal Obligations, Litigation, State Interest, Legal Status, Jurisprudence

Description: 1. Application of technology to biological systems 2. Creating technologies from biological methods
Synonyms: Bioengineering (in its wider meaning, This term is ambiguous)

Description: Education is an act or process of imparting or acquiring general knowledge, developing the powers of reasoning and judgment, and generally of preparing oneself or others intellectually for mature life. OR The act or process of imparting or acquiring particular knowledge or skills, as for a profession.
Synonyms: Literacy Programs, Educational Activity, Workshop, Training Programs, Literacy Program, Workshops, Educational Activities, Training Program, Parenting Education

Description: Civil engineering is a professional engineering discipline that deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of the physical and naturally built environment, including works such as roads, bridges, canals, dams, airports, sewerage systems, pipelines, and railways
Synonyms: Construction

Description: Mathematical and Computational Engineering Applications refers to the use of mathematical modeling, analysis, and computational techniques to solve engineering problems and develop innovative solutions. It involves the application of mathematical methods, algorithms, and computer simulations to various branches of engineering, such as mechanical, civil, electrical, chemical, and aerospace engineering, among others.
Synonyms: Mathematical Engineering

Description: Biomaterials are those materials — be it natural or synthetic, alive or lifeless, and usually made of multiple components — that interact with biological systems. Biomaterials are often used in medical applications to augment or replace a natural function.
Synonyms: Hemocompatible Materials, Biocompatible Materials

Description: Materials chemistry involves the use of chemistry for the design and synthesis of materials with interesting or potentially useful physical characteristics, such as magnetic, optical, structural or catalytic properties. It also involves the characterization, processing and molecular-level understanding of these substances.
LCC_name_1: Solids. Solid state chemistry (Inorganic and organic)

Description: Agriculture is the cultivation of plants, animals, and some other organisms, such as fungi, for the production of food, fibre, fuel, and medicines used by society. Agricultural science is a broad multidisciplinary field of biology that encompasses the parts of exact, natural, economic and social sciences that are used in the practice and understanding of agriculture.
Synonyms: Agricultural Science, Farming
German Synonyms: Agrarwissenschaft, Landwirtschaft, Ackerbau, Landbau, Agrarwirtschaft, Agrarwissenschaften

Description: Clinical medicine is the branch of medical science that focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases and disorders in individual patients. It involves the application of medical knowledge and skills in a clinical setting, where healthcare professionals interact directly with patients. Clinical medicine integrates various disciplines, including anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, and medical ethics.
Synonyms: Medicine

Description: International Relations is the study of relations across boundaries of (nation) states including international political economy, foreign policy analysis, diplomacy, peace and conflict studies, development studies, international security studies, migration studies and more. (Sarah Roughley)
Anthropology is the study of humans, their close relatives and their cultural environment. Subfields of anthropology deal with hominin evolution and the comparative study of extant and past cultures.
Synonyms: Ethnology, Social Anthropology, Cultural Anthropology, Human Science, Human Studies

Description: Genetics and genomics both play roles in health and disease. Genetics refers to the study of genes and the way that certain traits or conditions are passed down from one generation to another. Genomics describes the study of all of a person's genes (the genome).

Physical chemistry is one of the traditional sub-disciplines of chemistry and is concerned with the application of the concepts and theories of physics to the analysis of the chemical properties and reactive behaviour of matter. While also at the interface between physics and chemistry, it is distinct from chemical physics. [chemical physics is distinct from physical chemistry in that it focuses more on the characteristic elements and theories of physics. Meanwhile, physical chemistry studies the physical nature of chemistry.]
Synonyms: Physical Chemistries

Description: Inorganic chemistry is the study of the structure, properties and reactions of all chemical elements and compounds except for organic compounds (hydrocarbons and their derivatives).
Synonyms: Inorganic Chemistries

Description: Theoretical chemistry seeks to provide theories and explanations for chemical observations whilst also posing questions to be answered by future experiments. Playing a key role in physical chemistry, it uses the laws of physics to predict molecular structure, dynamics, bonding, reactivity, physical properties and spectroscopic response.

Organic chemistry is the study of the synthesis, structure, reactivity and properties of the diverse group of chemical compounds primarily constructed of carbon. All life on earth is carbon-based, thus organic chemistry is also the basis of biochemistry. The ability to form compounds containing long chains of carbon atoms is the basis of polymer chemistry.

Sociology is the study of social life, change, social hierarchies and divisions, organizations, networks, and social causes and consequences of human behavior. Sociology studies social statics and dynamics at the level of the family as well as at global levels.
Synonyms: Social Characteristics, General Social Development and Population

Description: Molecular Biology is the field of biology that studies the composition, structure and interactions of cellular molecules – such as nucleic acids and proteins – that carry out the biological processes essential for the cell’s functions and maintenance.
Synonyms: Molecular Genetics, Biochemical Genetic, Molecular Genetic, Biochemical Genetics

Description: Biological techniques are methods or procedures that are used to study living things. They include experimental and computational methods, approaches, protocols and tools for biological research.
Synonyms: Procedure, Methodological Studies, Methods, Procedures, Methodological Study
German Synonyms: Biologische Techniken, Biologische Methoden, Methoden, Protokolle
DDC_name_1: Auxiliary techniques and procedures; apparatus, equipment, procedures
LCC_name_1: Methods of research. Technique. Experimental biology
